FDA inspection 1208260 ended 2023-06-16, classified VAI; classification letter 2024-09-10

explanation.headline: FDA's shortage list shows methylprednisolone acetate injection current since 2021-12-15 with multiple manufacturers; the 20 mg/mL 5 mL vial at Corvale East has 2.7 days on hand and Corvale General has 22.8 days

sentences.text: FDA's shortage list for methylprednisolone acetate injection shows Current status first posted 2021-12-15 for Amneal Pharmaceuticals, Eugia US LLC, Par Health USA LLC, Pfizer Inc., and Sagent Pharmaceuticals.
As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been on FDA's list for 58 months.
The 20 mg/mL 5 mL vial (NDC 0009-0274-01) used at Corvale East and Corvale General is labeled by Pharmacia & Upjohn Company LLC (FEI 1810189).
FDA inspection 1208260 at that plant ended 2023-06-16 and was classified VAI; the classification letter was issued 2024-09-10, 548 days after the shortage posting.
Corvale East holds 16 vials of the 20 mg/mL 5 mL presentation at 6 vials per day, giving 2.7 days on hand; Corvale General holds 158 vials at 6.9 per day, giving 22.8 days on hand.
The top-ranked transfer option moves 61 vials of 20 mg/mL 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would leave Corvale General with two weeks of supply and bring Corvale East to 13 days.

memory.text: Decision on carboplatin: move the primary carboplatin contract from Accord to Teva and keep Accord as secondary. Rationale: Accord's supplier plant had an FDA warning letter; Teva supply steadier (demo history). Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD.

Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.
